note: سنگھ is most commonly encountered in Urdu as Singh, a Sikh/South Asian surname/title/name element. The Sanskrit-derived 'lion' sense is etymological; Leo/constellation is not a useful core Urdu gloss.
چونکہ is a subordinating conjunction meaning because/since. 'Closed-class' is too vague.
ذہن centrally means mind/intellect/mental faculty. 'Wit; genius' are secondary and should not replace the basic learner senses.
بجے is used in clock-time expressions for o'clock and is also a verb form of بجنا ('rings/sounds') depending on construction. The source gives only the clock use.
چہرے is an inflected form of چہرہ and must state face/faces rather than only inflection labels.
تحفظ centrally means protection/safeguarding/preservation/security/conservation. 'Learning by heart, committing to memory' is confusion with حفظ and should be removed.
اوقات is the plural of وقت and very commonly means times/hours/periods; it can also mean circumstances/status/means in idioms. The core temporal sense is missing.
proposed_english: times; hours; periods; circumstances/status; means/capacity (idiomatic, context-dependent)

note: علاقہ centrally means area/region/locality/territory. The source's 'area of a shape; affinity; connection' misses the everyday geographic meaning.
نہایت very commonly functions adverbially as very/extremely/exceedingly and also means end/limit. The source omits the dominant intensifier use.
لگ is the stem/imperative base of لگنا meaning attach/be attached/seem/begin/cost depending on construction. 'Content word' is not a POS.
proposed_english: attach; seem; begin; be attached; cost (stem of لگنا, context-dependent)

note: سمجھ is the noun understanding and also the verb stem/imperative 'understand!'. The source lists only the noun.
Rekhta gives livelihood/subsistence/employment as central senses alongside economy.
proposed_english: economy; economic condition; livelihood; subsistence; employment

note: اگرچہ means although/even though/though. Bare 'even' is not the correct standalone English equivalent.
Modern Urdu commonly writes the English loan ball as بال, especially in sports; Cambridge and Urdu usage sources explicitly attest this same spelling.
proposed_english: hair; wing; child; ball (English loan, especially sports, context-dependent)

note: روانہ means departed/set off/dispatched/sent off and functions adjectivally/participially. 'Pass, permit' is source noise and should be removed.
proposed_english: departed; set off; dispatched; sent off

note: قدم centrally means foot/step/footstep. The qidam reading 'antiquity/permanence' is a distinct learned homograph; the source omits the basic 'foot' meaning.
proposed_english: foot; step; footstep; antiquity/oldness (different vocalization, learned use)
